issues.description: GKE detection via name prefix 'gke-' is unreliable and bypassable
issues.detail: The check downgrades multi-NIC findings from FAIL to MANUAL when `instance.name.startswith('gke-')`. Instance names are user-controllable, so an operator (or attacker) can trivially evade this security control by naming a VM with the `gke-` prefix. The correct signal for GKE-managed nodes is the `goog-gke-node` label or instance metadata (e.g., the `cluster-name` metadata key), not the name. Use labels/metadata to identify GKE-managed instances.

issues.description: Instance with 0 network interfaces silently reports PASS
issues.detail: The else branch covers `interface_count == 0` and falls through with the default `status = 'PASS'` while emitting a status_extended that says the VM has no network interfaces. That is semantically wrong: an instance with no NICs is not 'a single network interface'. Either skip it, mark it MANUAL, or treat it as a data-quality issue. As written, the report claims compliance for an anomalous state.

issues.description: metadata.json and check docstring disagree on status outcomes
issues.detail: The check docstring documents three outcomes (PASS, MANUAL, FAIL) including GKE-aware handling. The metadata.json Description/Risk/Notes never mention MANUAL or describe the GKE-name carve-out — only that GKE/appliances 'may legitimately require multiple interfaces'. Operators reading the metadata will not know the check silently downgrades GKE-named instances. Document the MANUAL state and the precise carve-out rule (and what label/metadata it keys on after the P1 fix above).

issues.description: PR title/description references 'multiple_network_interfaces' but implementation uses 'single_network_interface'
issues.detail: The PR title is 'add check to detect VMs with multiple network interfaces' and the description's 'New Check' header says `compute_instance_multiple_network_interfaces/`, but every file, the CHANGELOG entry, the metadata CheckID, and the hub URL use `compute_instance_single_network_interface`. The shipped name is consistent internally; only the PR description is stale. No code change needed, but reviewers should confirm the intended canonical name before merge.

issues.description: Description in PR claims only PASS/FAIL, but code introduces a MANUAL status
issues.detail: The PR description's bulleted outcome list shows only PASS and FAIL. The implementation adds a third state (MANUAL) for GKE-named instances. Behavior beyond the documented contract makes it harder for downstream consumers (dashboards, suppressions, scoring) to plan. Either drop the MANUAL branch or update the description and metadata to match.

issues.description: Tests do not cover the 0-interface branch or the network/subnetwork URL parsing
issues.detail: The new tests cover single, two, three, four-NIC, and GKE-named cases, but not an instance with `network_interfaces=[]`. Given the bug flagged above (0 NICs reports PASS), a test would have caught it. Additionally, the service-level test only asserts counts (`len(...) == 1` and `== 0`) and does not verify that `network`/`subnetwork` URLs are correctly truncated to the trailing path segment in `_get_instances`.

issues.description: NetworkInterface drops project/region context from network and subnetwork URLs
issues.detail: `interface.get('network', '').split('/')[-1]` keeps only the trailing name. For multi-NIC lateral-movement analysis (the stated purpose of the check), the project and region embedded in the full self-link are exactly the signal that distinguishes a benign in-VPC second NIC from a cross-project bridge. Consider preserving the full self-link or adding `project`/`region` fields.

`network_interfaces: list[NetworkInterface] = []` uses a mutable default. Pydantic v1/v2 copies defaults per instance so this is generally safe, but the surrounding model uses similar patterns (e.g., `disks_encryption=[]` exists already by inference). No action required if the project is on Pydantic; flagging only because a stricter linter may complain.

dissents.topic: Should the GKE carve-out exist at all?

positions.position: Keep the carve-out but base it on labels/metadata. False positives on GKE node pools are a real operator pain and will drive the check to be disabled. MANUAL is the right compromise.

Drop the carve-out entirely. Security checks should not have name-based escape hatches because the signal is attacker-controllable. Let users suppress per-resource if needed; do not bake bypasses into the check.
0 NICs is an anomaly and should be MANUAL or INFO — claiming PASS is misleading.
An instance with no NICs trivially satisfies 'not multiple NICs', so PASS is defensible and the status_extended already clarifies the state. Leave as-is.

review.summary: The PR adds a useful GCP check with reasonable structure and good test coverage for the happy paths, but it has two substantive issues that should be addressed before merge. First, the GKE bypass uses `instance.name.startswith('gke-')`, which is attacker-controllable and undermines the control's value; GKE-managed nodes should be identified via the `goog-gke-node` label or instance metadata. Second, an instance with zero network interfaces falls through to PASS, which is semantically wrong and not covered by tests. There are also documentation drift issues (the PR description and metadata.json don't reflect the MANUAL state or the GKE carve-out) and a missed opportunity in the data model where network/subnetwork URLs are truncated to their trailing segment, discarding project/region context that is precisely the signal needed for lateral-movement analysis. Nothing here is a hard P0 blocker, but the GKE-naming bypass is close — it materially weakens a security check.
